departments[].task_generation_locations.runtime_default: No department assignment; retain category routing. No drop-off zone by default.
departments[].task_generation_locations.meaning: Per-category service destinations or pickups and optional intermediate drop-off-zone locations.
departments[].task_generation_locations.precedence: Modern pickup_dropoff_locations wins over locations; dropoff_zone_locations wins over drop_off_zone_locations, including explicit empty lists. A category scalar/list is service shorthand. A scalar is one literal name, never comma-separated. Trim whitespace and deduplicate in first-seen order. A nonempty service assignment replaces category pickup or dropoff according to department_location_role; zones apply to delivery handoff with a service destination.
departments[].task_generation_locations.editor_behaviour: Import canonicalizes effective selections without losing aliases or category metadata. Accept and deletion preserve explicit empty modern lists, so shadowed aliases cannot be revived. Unlisted categories survive editing. Placements remain provisional through child OK and are committed with department Save in one undoable change; cancellation leaves project data untouched. Invalid or conflicting pending locations reject atomically and remain available for correction.
departments[].task_generation_locations.validation: Known assignment fields must be a string or list of strings. Null, booleans, numeric names and object-valued names reject import/runtime/preflight. Effective missing location references block managed Project Checks; shadowed alias names are not effective references. Pending locations require unique nonblank names, finite nonboolean coordinates and whole floors.
departments[].task_generation_locations.limitations: Empty service lists retain category routing rather than disable demand. Unknown category assignments may remain unused. Raw simulation validates shape but managed Project Checks supplies missing-location preflight. Legacy waste_pickup_locations is retained without implicit migration to modern categories. Provisional locations are bare points requiring connectivity and capacity configuration; general stale modal edits, sharing/deleting provisional owners and full report/stock reconciliation remain open.

departments.meaning: Department records used by demand generation and editable markers.
departments.precedence: A nonblank ID wins; otherwise use the name, consistently in dynamic and legacy waste generation. Group membership suppresses ordinary per-department overrides. Identity changes explicitly remap group members, override keys and static task department IDs without editing graph routes.
departments.editor_behaviour: Atomic replacement validates the complete candidate. Canvas ID edits update the original row; list edits track successive identity changes. Nested department data is copied for cancellation. Referenced deletions and conflicting override destinations are rejected without mutation. Coordinate moves retain precision. Graph labels take precedence over colliding department labels and managed checks require correction.
departments.validation: Supplied IDs/names must be strings without surrounding whitespace. Nonblank effective IDs and display names are unique. Missing identity remains an editable draft but cannot run. Supplied coordinates must be finite nonboolean numbers; floors must be whole. Group members must be a list of nonblank unique strings. Unknown department assignments receive acknowledgeable no-work warnings.
departments.limitations: Labels are not routing locations. Does not remap arbitrary metadata, external files or frozen results. Existing missing group/override references can remain intentionally acknowledged; unused invalid references do not prove demand coverage. Category-location aliases and provisional placement are covered by their separate contract; full reference/deletion coverage and stale modal edits remain open.

departments[].enabled.meaning: Enable department opening periods and their generated demand.
departments[].enabled.precedence: Explicit end clock wins over legacy hours. Equal clocks and zero legacy hours retain the full-day convention. Earlier end is next day. Department openings constrain generated releases. Legacy waste rate is alpha*beds + beta*(turnover/operating_hours) + gamma*staff; modern category rates are separate.
departments[].enabled.editor_behaviour: Overnight and nonmidnight full-day imports materialise the correct end clock without shortening the window. Repeated normalisation preserves the interval. Dialogs preserve fractional values, legacy coefficients and unedited metadata; invalid values do not produce a result. Upsert validates before mutation.
departments[].enabled.validation: Enabled must be a JSON boolean. Demographics and coefficients must be finite nonnegative numbers; numeric strings accepted, booleans/null rejected. Hours are within 0..24. Clocks accept legacy whole-hour strings or H:MM/HH:MM, blank fallback, and 24:00 only for end. Days must be a list of abbreviated weekday keys, case-insensitive. Combined legacy hourly rate must remain finite.
departments[].enabled.limitations: Legacy empirical demand formula, not a validated clinical waste model. No automatic mapping to modern category demand or staff capacity. Identity/reference/floor/coordinate handling and complete department editing remain separate audit work. Minute rounding and equal-clock full-day convention retained; disable a department for no work. Partial horizons, full event/stock reconciliation and all mode interactions are not established by these references.

locations[].inventory_spaces[].length_m.meaning: Bay plan envelope; payload may rotate in plan for storage independently of its AMR carrying permissions
locations[].inventory_spaces[].length_m.precedence: Any AMR marker makes a bay AMR-only. Parent and effective slot references form the union of permitted AMR type/instance IDs. Slot amr_type overrides legacy amr, including an explicit empty modern value. Modern dimensions override legacy dimensional aliases, then numeric zero invokes outline/template inference; zero does not fall back to the overridden alias. Numeric strings use the same zero rule. Inferred plan extents resolve each point into local coordinates using its parent location; complete dx/dy wins over legacy x/y.
locations[].inventory_spaces[].length_m.editor_behaviour: Import and editing share AMR classification and alias precedence with runtime. Type compatibility recognises parent, union and instance restrictions. Bay edits preserve dimensions/metadata and zero uses shared inference. A zero-quantity robot type requires no charging bay.
locations[].inventory_spaces[].length_m.validation: Shared input checks reject unknown type tags, malformed values and nonfinite resolved envelopes. Runtime/preflight require effective AMR aliases to resolve. Zero bay dimensions are permitted for inference; unresolved zero plan extents, effectively unbounded height, mixed templates and unused payload-bay charger flags are visible warnings. Payload and AMR dimensions remain strictly positive.
locations[].inventory_spaces[].length_m.limitations: Partial storage model: envelopes are not polygon containment or swept clearance. AMR fit retains 1e-3 m tolerance and payload fit 1e-6 m. Mixed payload templates cannot make an AMR bay store payloads but can still influence inferred height. The legacy 999999 m height remains an explicit warning. Initial cross-type/instance matching is covered by the fleet references. Live fleet rematching, charger throughput, geometric parking and all dialog precision still need acceptance work. Initial occupancy is not stock seeding; physical packing/stacking remains unsupported. Report capacity counts exclude AMR bays and use the same nominal envelope; count-only comparisons explicitly lack dimensional evidence. Drawn inventory area excludes AMR outlines and does not fabricate area for dimension-only bays. Matching is hypothetical nominal capacity, not live availability or execution proof.

building.charge_locations.meaning: Ordered charging-location names, supplied as a JSON list or legacy comma-separated string. Duplicates are removed in effective resolution without editing the source input.
building.charge_locations.precedence: Modern list/legacy CSV wins when nonempty; otherwise legacy charge_location, then first location. building.charge_locations.validation: Malformed name containers reject on import/run. Effective unknown locations block running; unresolved draft references remain editable. Shared and instance-restricted bays count once across the whole fleet. Insufficient simultaneous initial chargers is an acknowledgeable constraint, not malformed input.
building.charge_locations.editor_behaviour: Editor and runtime use the same location resolver and footprint/restriction compatibility. Location rename updates list, CSV and legacy charging references. Project Checks uses distinct-robot matching and reports legacy location-only starts explicitly; old string validation remains a compatibility adapter.
building.charge_locations.limitations: Initial matching verifies compatibility and distinct occupancy, not queue geometry, swept clearance, charger throughput or energy sufficiency. Unmatched robots retain the legacy start at a location point. Runtime return/charge dispatch is separate and does not globally rematch all live robots. Full scheduling, performance and physical parking acceptance remain open.
